findings.title: Worker shutdown waits out the Reddit pacer, so docker stop -t 35 / Railway usually SIGKILLs it before claims and the fleet row are released
findings.evidence: stop() sets running=false and only wakes the runner's own idle sleep (runner.ts:68-69). The poll iteration spends most of its time in pacer.acquire(), whose setTimeout can't be interrupted (pacing.ts:50-52). With REDDIT_MAX_RPM=1, minGap is 60 s, while each fetch takes about 1 s plus the 1 s busy pause. After acquire returns, pollOnce still claims up to 20 subreddits and fetches them (20 s timeout) without checking for shutdown. index.ts awaits every loop's `stopped` before releaseAllClaims/deregister. deploy-workers.sh gives the container 35 s before SIGKILL.
findings.failure_scenario: During scripts/deploy-workers.sh, each VM gets SIGTERM while its poll loop is about 40 s into a 60 s pacer wait, which is the common case. The loop wakes after about 20 s, claims a batch and starts the fetch, and docker SIGKILLs it at 35 s. The batch stays claimed and invisible for the 5-minute CLAIM_TTL. Evaluate/notify claims held by the process are kept too. Its `workers` row is never deleted, and the new container gets a new hostname-pid id. About 10 minutes later the ops watch pages 'Reddit worker down: <old id>' for every redeployed VM. This is exactly what docs/debug-notes/signals-must-reach-node.md set out to prevent.
findings.proposed_fix: Give RedditPacer.acquire an AbortSignal, or a stopping flag the runner flips, and return false from pollOnce/Tracer.once when it's aborted before claiming. Also raise docker stop -t above minGap + FEED_TIMEOUT (for example 90).
findings.regression_test: Unit: start the poll loop with a fake pacer whose acquire blocks, call stop(), and assert `stopped` resolves without claimDueSubreddits being called.

findings.title: A worker running ALERT_TRANSPORT=console against the shared DB marks buyer targets notified without sending them; the deploy script defaults to console
findings.evidence: The console sender sets requiresRecipients=false and returns delivered=[...chatIds] (alerts.ts:63). notifyOnce therefore claims 'target' posts and calls markNotified, which is terminal. deploy-workers.sh writes ALERT_TRANSPORT=${ALERT_TRANSPORT:-console}, and secrets.env.example ships ALERT_TRANSPORT=console. Claims are fleet-wide, so whichever worker claims a target first decides whether buyers get it. Behaviour is pinned by tests/pipeline.test.ts:315. The index.ts:89-91 comment shows console mode is meant to keep a local process off prod's Telegram updates, but nothing keeps it off prod's notify queue.
findings.failure_scenario: The owner runs deploy-workers.sh with a secrets.env that leaves out ALERT_TRANSPORT, or a dev runs `pnpm dev` with ALERT_TRANSPORT=console against the prod DATABASE_URL. That worker wins the claim on roughly 1/N of the targets, prints them to docker logs and marks them notified. Buyers silently miss those leads. Analytics counts them as alerts with no reaction, and dedup parks their cross-posts as duplicates of an alert nobody saw.
findings.proposed_fix: Make console mode never claim 'target' rows when telegram_chat_ids is non-empty, or refuse to start in console mode when it is. Make deploy-workers.sh require ALERT_TRANSPORT explicitly, with no console default.
findings.regression_test: pipeline test: with telegram_chat_ids set, a console-transport notifyOnce leaves the target in status 'target'.

findings.title: The Railway worker has a fixed WORKER_ID, so during a redeploy overlap the old process's shutdown releases the new process's claims and lease and deletes its fleet row
findings.location: railway reddits-tracker/production service worker (eed8d23f) variable WORKER_ID; trackers/reddit/src/config.ts:100; src/claims.ts:383-389; src/heartbeat.ts:211-213; src/index.ts:318-325
findings.evidence: The worker service sets WORKER_ID, so every deployment of that service shares one id. README.md:75-76 notes that a Railway redeploy starts the new copy before the old one stops. On shutdown, releaseAllClaims(sql, workerId) clears every subreddit/post claim with claimed_by = that id and deletes its loop_leases row. removeWorker then deletes the shared workers row. The new process is already claiming under the same id.
findings.failure_scenario: A redeploy happens while the new worker is mid-notify on target P, or mid-evaluate. The old copy's shutdown nulls P's claim, an OCI worker claims P, and buyers get a second alert. The new worker's later markNotified is a no-op because claimed_by no longer matches, but its message ids are still inserted. The new worker's fleet row also vanishes until its next 30 s beat, and its comment_tracer lease is dropped. This needs the overlap to outlast the old process's loop drain; Railway's draining/overlap settings weren't checked.
findings.proposed_fix: Drop WORKER_ID from the Railway worker, or append a per-process suffix such as RAILWAY_DEPLOYMENT_ID/randomUUID to any configured WORKER_ID so ids stay unique per process.
findings.regression_test: claims test: two workers with the same id, one releaseAllClaims, assert the other's claim survives (fails today, which documents the hazard). Better: config test that the generated id is unique even when WORKER_ID is set.

findings.title: One unreadable subreddit fails its whole 20-sub multireddit batch, and the batch stays welded together through backoff
findings.evidence: A 403/401 or HTML page is treated as an IP block and backs off the whole process (pacer.recordBlocked). A 404 becomes 'error'. In both cases releaseSubredditFailure gives every claimed sub the same consecutive_errors and next_poll_at. claimDueSubreddits orders by next_poll_at, so the same set is claimed together again and keeps failing up to the 30-minute cap.
findings.failure_scenario: If Reddit answers a multireddit containing a banned or private sub with 403/404 (unverified live), every watched sub in that batch is polled at most every 30 min, and the worker's IP backoff grows to 15 min. The fleet effectively stops discovering posts.
findings.proposed_fix: On a batch failure, retry its subs singly (or bisect) before backing off everyone. Treat 404 as per-sub and don't feed it to the IP pacer.
findings.regression_test: poll test with a feed mock that 404s when one named sub is in the path: the other subs still get polled within one interval.

findings.title: The 300 s claim TTL can expire inside one evaluate/notify batch, allowing a duplicate LLM call or a duplicate buyer alert
findings.evidence: Evaluate claims 3 posts and handles them serially, with up to two 60 s OpenRouter calls each while a candidate runs: 360 s worst case. Notify claims 5 and sends to every chat serially, at up to 20 s timeout + 60 s retry_after + 20 s per chat. Claims aren't renewed during the batch.
findings.failure_scenario: Under a Telegram flood-wait or a slow OpenRouter, a later post in the batch passes 300 s. Another worker re-claims it and sends or judges it again, and the first worker's mark is silently dropped by the claimed_by guard.
findings.proposed_fix: Re-claim (touch claimed_at) before each post, or process claimed rows one at a time.
findings.regression_test: Unit with fake slow sender asserting claimed_at is refreshed per post.

findings.title: A group upgraded to a supergroup still fails every alert silently until a person edits telegram_chat_ids
findings.evidence: sendOne keeps only `description` and drops parameters.migrate_to_chat_id. The debug note from 2026-08-16 records the outage and says so, but the code still doesn't handle it.
findings.failure_scenario: A buyer group is upgraded. Every alert fails, each target parks as 'failed' after 5 attempts, and the only signal is the error digest.
findings.proposed_fix: Surface migrate_to_chat_id in the failure and, on the api, rewrite the setting (or at least log it as an error with the new id).
findings.regression_test: telegram test: 400 with migrate_to_chat_id reports the new id.

findings.title: The api's user-notify loop, the sole buyer-alert sender while the user session is live, never trips the 'failing' page
findings.evidence: Only worker loops go through registry.wrap. The api's user-notify/reads/reactions loops aren't wrapped, so consecutiveFailures never increments for them. While the api renews user_sender_at, workers stand down (notify.ts:48).
findings.failure_scenario: Suppose the user session sends fail and the bot fallback also fails, or the notify DB queries throw. Buyer alerts stop and posts park as failed, but the ops watch sends only digest lines, never a 'notify failing on api' page.
findings.proposed_fix: Wrap the api's user-notify in registry.wrap('notify', …), or add 'user-notify' to LOOP_NAMES without exposing it in the ERP loops contract.
findings.regression_test: heartbeat test asserting api notify failures raise loop_failures.

findings.title: OCI workers accept SSH from 0.0.0.0/0 by default while holding a full-privilege public prod DB URL
findings.evidence: ssh_ingress_cidr defaults to 0.0.0.0/0, and the example keeps that. Each VM's /opt/reddits_tracker/.env holds the Railway Postgres public proxy URL as the owner role.
findings.failure_scenario: If one VM is compromised, for example through an unpatched sshd, an attacker gets read/write on the whole tracker DB, including settings that steer where alerts go.
findings.proposed_fix: Restrict ssh_ingress_cidr to the office/VPN, and give workers a least-privilege DB role.

findings.title: deploy-workers.sh interpolates GHCR_READ_TOKEN into the ssh command line
findings.evidence: "echo '${GHCR_READ_TOKEN}' | sudo docker login …" is built as the ssh argument, so the token sits in the local process list for the length of each ssh call.
findings.failure_scenario: Another local user or process can read the PAT from `ps`. Impact is limited because the token is read:packages only.
findings.proposed_fix: Pipe the token over stdin, as the env file already is (printf | ssh 'docker login --password-stdin').

findings.title: API bearer token compared with !==
findings.evidence: A plain string comparison on a public Railway domain (api-production-1c1d.up.railway.app).
findings.failure_scenario: This is a theoretical timing side channel. It isn't practical over the internet, but it's free to fix.
